t.7.55.1: Thus addressed by Rāma, Śatrughna, endowed with valour, was overcome by deep embarrassment and spoke very softly.
t.7.55.2: Your command must certainly be carried out, O bull among men, for your command, O illustrious one, is hard to transgress. Here I am, O king, ready to do whatever you wish, O bull among men.
t.7.55.3: When the heroic and great-souled Śatrughna had spoken thus, Rāma, greatly delighted, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa and to Bharata as well.
t.7.55.4: Attentively bring the materials for the consecration. This very day I shall consecrate that tiger among men, the invincible one.
t.7.55.5: O Kākutsthas, by my command bring here the family priest, the townsfolk and the officiating priests, and all my ministers as well.
t.7.55.7: Then the consecration of the great-souled Śatrughna went forward, a splendid rite that brought great joy to Rāghava and to the city.
t.7.55.6: Having understood the king's command, the great chariot-warrior acted accordingly. Placing the preparations for the consecration and the family priest at the forefront, they entered the royal palace, which was like the abode of Puraṃdara.
t.7.55.8: Then Rāghava, placing the consecrated Śatrughna on his lap, spoke sweet words, filling him with splendour.
t.7.55.9: This unfailing, divine arrow, conqueror of enemy cities, is yours; with it, O gentle one, O Raghunandana, you will slay Lavaṇa.
t.7.55.10: This arrow, O Kākutstha, was created when the self-born, unconquered god, whom neither the suras nor the asuras could see, lay upon the great ocean.
t.7.55.11: This supreme arrow, invisible to all beings, was created by him, overcome with wrath, O hero, for the destruction of the two evil-souled ones, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, when they were bent on destruction.
t.7.55.12: Desiring to create the three worlds, he slew those two in battle with this foremost of arrows, and then he made the worlds.
t.7.55.13: This arrow, O Śatrughna, was not released by me before, when I sought the slaying of Rāvaṇa, for fear that great terror would arise among all beings.
t.7.55.14: And that great trident of his, the supreme weapon of Madhu, which was given by the great-souled Tryambaka for the destruction of enemies.
t.7.55.16: But whenever anyone, eager for battle, challenges him, then that rākṣasa takes up the trident and reduces him to ashes.
t.7.55.15: Having laid it down in the dwelling, where it is worshipped again and again, and having looked about in all directions, he obtains his own food.
t.7.55.17: So you, tiger among men, must stand at the gate with your weapons ready and face him while he is still without his weapon and has not yet entered the city.
t.7.55.18: O bull among men, O mighty-armed one, challenge the rākṣasa to battle while he has not yet entered his dwelling; then you will slay him.
t.7.55.19: If it is done otherwise, he will be impossible to slay; but if it is done in this way, O hero, he will meet his destruction.
t.7.55.20: All this has been told to you, along with the reversal concerning the trident, for what has been done by the glorious Śitikaṇṭha is indeed hard to overcome.
